name: @examples/consumer-project
//: The minimal ordinary business project #99 asks a new Agent to be able to work in: project
source, `forguncy.config.ts`, the Skill and an authorized MCP connection, and nothing else.
The dependency list is deliberate, and each entry is a fact about how this Cell is built:
- `@app/consumer-ui` is a workspace package imported by name. The compiler flattens its source
into the Cell artifact (#14), so it is *source* rather than a runtime module and never
receives a dependency decision or appears in `frontendLibraries`.
- `@forguncy-react-workspace/runtime` is the façade the Cell calls for data, permissions and
commands (#27/#82). It is also flattened, so the same source works under `vp dev` and in the
- `es-toolkit` is the installed ESM package decided `inline` (#10): the compiler bundles the
package's own code, and the decision is recorded in `fgc.lock.json` by the Skill's `record`
rather than committed here (see `dependencies/es-toolkit.decision.json` and the README).
`react` is deliberately NOT a dependency: it is decided `host`, the host bridge intercepts the
specifier before Node resolution runs, and installing it would be a silent escape hatch for a
broken interception — the rule `examples/host-antd/package.json` records at length.
`vite-plus` and `dev-harness` are devDependencies because they are what `vp dev` assembles;
`core` supplies `defineForguncyConfig` in the committed config; `cell-project` supplies the
`fgc-cell` binary the three scripts below run. None of them is reachable from the Cell's own
//scripts: `vp dev` is the local loop and is deliberately not wrapped here (#22/#23).
`record` runs the dependency-selection Skill's deterministic half against this project: the
probe measures es-toolkit, the lock records the inline decision, and the evidence is written
beside it. It is the one step that needs the Skill; a consumer outside this repository runs the
same command from wherever their installed Skill lives.
`build`, `plan` and `sync` are the public verbs (#99). `build` and `plan` make no remote call;
`sync` requires `--port`, because an authorized designer connection is the caller's and this
`fgc.lock.json` and `fgc-evidence/` are NOT committed, and that is a measured decision rather
than an omission: a record's `probedWith.installGraph` digests the installed tree, and this
repository's own `vp test`/`vp dev` runs write caches under `node_modules`, so a committed
record reported `install-graph-changed` the moment it was exercised. What *is* committed is the
decision input under `dependencies/` — the reviewable half — and `pnpm record` is what turns it
into a measurement of the machine running it (#94).
Both are git-ignored so a fresh clone and a worked checkout look the same.
